CAST, NOT SAILED: ticket an-emission-is-one-file-named-by-its-pointer (CairnCommons/tickets/, commit a117500), child (5) of every-boundary-crossing-lands-in-the-logs-tree. Cursor [TICKETME]; `chain an-emission-is-one-file-named-by-its-pointer` is ALL-None — no chart taken, /sail's step 0 will make it. Sorted door passed first fire, berth ~/.cairn/devices/skill_block/0/berths/sorted/sorted-20260819T103100-48f476d1392a.json.

WHAT IT SETTLES, and it is two halves in one node because they are one file's grain. (a) One emission = one FILE, not a row appended to ~/.cairn/logs/<device>/<instance>/diagnostics.jsonl. Akien 2026-08-19: 'i was expecting to see timestamp.inference.task.json or some such'. (b) The pointer gets thin enough to BE a filename. The join: the name he asked for carries the task, so the file cannot be named until the pointer is short enough to name it — a 10,078-char pointer is not a filename on any filesystem here.

MEASURED THIS SESSION, and the census is what made this a leaf ticket rather than a corpus sweep: 37 live emit sites across 18 files; pointer-length medians bus 32, charter 29, ground_loop 9, tester 70, trouble 44 — and inference_domain 1,171 (max 10,078), 85% of that trail's 273,421 bytes. The fat pointer is a POPULATION OF ONE, three lines: cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py:319, :373, :408, all pointer=canonical.

ALSO MEASURED, dissolving the contradiction Akien named and self-caught: 140 emissions / 68 distinct pointers in inference_domain's trail; gate sequences only miss->hit (66) or miss->hit->hit->hit (2); inter-emission gaps on a shared pointer min 3.2s, median 282s, max 4,348s, zero under 1s. ONE INFERENCE CALL = EXACTLY ONE EMISSION. The pointer is the PROMPT, not the call — repeats are later calls asking the same question.

OWNERSHIP FACT found by reading the design before defending the code: the logs ADDRESS is Akien's 2026-08-18 ruling; the append-JSONL SHAPE was CC's decision inside a-record-reaches-disk (PROVED, closed 2026-08-12) and has never been at his gate. The two sit in adjacent sentences of one docstring in cairn/tools/base/breadcrumb_log.py with nothing marking which is which.

BLAST RADIUS counted before any build: 30 sites spell diagnostics.jsonl or RECORD_NAME. Code is few — 1 writer (breadcrumb_log.py), 1 reader contract, 3 proofs, 1 fixture, 1 probe. The rest is load-bearing prose in four charters/docstrings, so charter deltas are owed in the same act and each pokes recompile_gate.sh.
next_direction:
/sail an-emission-is-one-file-named-by-its-pointer. Its falsifier has 5 clauses; clause (2) is the one that earns the change because it is the property the current shape CANNOT have: stamp two emission files at 31 and 1 days back, run ONE `find <root> -mtime +30 -delete`, exactly the old one goes and the young one stands. Today that command takes a device's whole history or nothing — which is precisely the why Akien gave for the address ruling ('easy to delete everything in the logs tree over 30 days old in one go') and the shape does not deliver it.

BOUND INTO THE SAME ACT, do not let it drift to a follow-up: cairn/devices/inference_domain/probes/an_inference_call_logs_that_it_started.py:104 joins on the fat pointer (`str(rec.get('pointer'))` counted against store canonicals). Left unchanged past the digest it compares two vocabularies and reports a disagreement that is an artifact of this ticket, not a finding.

TWO THINGS AT AKIEN'S GATE, neither blocking the build (MY READ, not ratified):
1. The filename's exact spelling. He said 'timestamp.inference.task.json OR SOME SUCH' — the segments are his, the grain is not, and I will not invent the separator character or the timestamp precision without him.
2. A rule I could not find written anywhere and am proposing in the ticket's distinctions_recorded (1): A PROVED NODE'S FALSIFIER MAY BE RE-SPELLED BY A LATER NODE WITHOUT BEING RETRACTED, PROVIDED THE LATER NODE CARRIES THE EARLIER SUBSTANCE FORWARD EXPLICITLY. Live case: an-inference-call-logs-that-it-started proved 2026-08-18 naming diagnostics.jsonl and matching trail-to-meter by canonical TEXT; both spellings change here. I did not edit its record (Law 7), and clause (5) of the new falsifier carries its substance forward. Without the rule the corpus freezes at its first spelling, or a proof quietly stops meaning what it proved.
